scope: Focused, non-exhaustive primary-source review of personalized, task-oriented and decision-focused summarization relevant to Nubble; selected close precedents and evaluation methods, not a systematic review.
search_routes: Targeted Firecrawl web search and primary-page scrape
search_queries: personalized summarization task oriented summaries user goals decision support news
decision focused summarization actionable intelligence business strategic report summarization
query focused summarization user model information need decision making

evidence_legend.A: Canonical primary metadata and relevant primary full-text passages read; not necessarily whole-paper cover-to-cover review.
evidence_legend.B: Primary method passages or abstract available but one bibliographic/empirical component remains unverified.

sources.title: Decision-Focused Summarization
sources.version_read: arXiv v1 (2021-09-14); canonical EMNLP metadata verified
sources.evidence_level: A: canonical proceedings metadata plus primary methods/evaluation passages
evidence_sections: §2 decision faithfulness, representativeness and greedy extractive selection
sources.core_method: Selects a subset of input sentences to preserve a supervised predictor's decision, represent the sentence-level decision distribution, and avoid textual redundancy.
sources.closest_overlap: Explicitly makes downstream decisions, rather than generic textual salience, the summarization objective; controls summary length.
sources.defensible_difference: Nubble can test a linked presentation of evidence, contextual relevance and conditional implication/action options. DecSum does not operationalize a professional user's changing context or a structured act/verify/monitor/no-action choice.
sources.verified_findings: In the inspected setup, humans predicted which of two restaurants would receive a higher future rating from summaries of their first ten reviews. Authors report DecSum was the only evaluated method above chance; do not generalize to business or clinical decisions.
sources.numeric_result: Not reported here: the retrieved passages do not expose the results table and test details.
sources.limitations: Supervised prediction model and a Yelp proxy task; faithfulness to model output is not factual correctness or action quality. Author reports grammaticality/coherence cost.
sources.nubble_upgrade: Compare decision correctness, material-risk omissions and abstention calibration under equal total reading time; retain a strong extractive baseline.
sources.citation_caution: Some later papers miscite DecSum as 2021.emnlp-main.47. That DOI is Text2Mol. Correct ID is .10.

sources.title: PersonalSum: A User-Subjective Guided Personalized Summarization Dataset for Large Language Models
sources.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37, Datasets and Benchmarks
sources.access_level: Open primary full text; dataset license reported CC BY-NC 4.0
sources.evidence_level: A: proceedings metadata plus primary methods, human evaluation and limitations passages
sources.core_method: Human-authored personalized news summaries are linked to source sentences and user profiles; experiments condition on user history and entity, plot and article-structure preferences.
sources.closest_overlap: The same article can have different valid reader-specific summaries; source-sentence links and user-context personalization precede Nubble.
sources.defensible_difference: The dataset concerns preferred article content, not explicit conditional implications, feasible actions or measured decision benefit.
sources.verified_findings: The authors' small human evaluation used 50 samples and three Norwegian-speaking student evaluators. They report that entity/topic preference is insufficient to explain user preference, with plot and structure also contributing.
sources.numeric_result: No transferable effect size reported here.
sources.limitations: Limited training data and assigned rather than user-selected articles; preference matching is not decision usefulness.
sources.nubble_upgrade: Collect actual current task, prior knowledge, constraints and explicit goal rather than rely on an occupation label or keywords. Annotate summary propositions with source evidence and collect reader-owned labels.

sources.title: SumRecom: A Personalized Summarization Approach by Learning from Users' Feedback
sources.publication_status: Preprint; journal or conference publication not verified
sources.evidence_level: B: canonical research-index metadata plus primary method and human-study passages; venue not independently established
sources.core_method: Learns concept preferences through active pairwise feedback and uses inverse reinforcement learning to generate a personalized summary without requiring a reference summary at use time.
sources.closest_overlap: Human-in-the-loop personalization and cognitive burden are already explicit design concerns; summaries are evaluated with a fixed 75-word length.
sources.defensible_difference: Preference optimization does not supply a separate conditional interpretation/action layer or evaluate feasibility and decision benefit.
sources.verified_findings: Primary text describes 15 AMT workers, ten DUC document clusters and an 83% preference selection result for the personalized summary among five alternatives. This is a small preference study, not evidence of better downstream decisions.
sources.numeric_result: 83% preference selection as reported by authors; denominator and exact uncertainty beyond the described participant sample not verified.
sources.limitations: Requires interaction to infer interest; additional user elicitation consumes attention and its cost must be counted.
sources.nubble_upgrade: Count onboarding, feedback, source verification and follow-up time in the attention budget, not just output words.

sources.title: Does This Summary Answer My Question? Modeling Query-Focused Summary Readers with Rational Speech Acts
sources.evidence_level: A: arXiv metadata plus primary methods, experiment and limitation passages
sources.core_method: Generates ten query-focused candidate summaries, then reranks using a reader model's ability to reconstruct an answer, combined with generator likelihood.
sources.closest_overlap: Explicit reader utility is part of generation; preserving reader-relevant answers is not new.
sources.defensible_difference: Tests question answering from a summary rather than producing conditional, actionable implications for a bounded professional decision.
sources.verified_findings: Authors report better reference alignment from reader-aware reranking but explicitly acknowledge lack of an extensive human evaluation and imperfect validity of overlap and learned metrics.
sources.limitations: Synthetic QA answers introduce noise; BART/Llama 3 only; no direct evidence of actual reader task performance.
sources.nubble_upgrade: Use a reader-comprehension check, but validate it against blinded human decisions and risk recognition rather than treating an LLM reconstruction score as ground truth.

sources.title: Personalized Chain-of-Thought Summarization of Financial News for Investor Decision Support
sources.venue: arXiv; author comments state Proceedings of ICDM Workshops
sources.publication_status: Workshop claim in arXiv comments; independent proceedings DOI not verified
sources.evidence_level: A for framework/method; B for publication status; empirical claims intentionally restricted
evidence_sections: §III-D relevance, key insights and three investment actions
sources.core_method: Raw financial-news PDF extraction → initial summaries → financial metadata/enhanced summaries → keyword-conditioned relevance, implications and exactly three investment recommendations; Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 with 2,048-token truncation.
sources.closest_overlap: Very direct precedent for personalized summary → implications → recommendations. A summary plus 'So What' is not independently novel.
sources.defensible_difference: Nubble must test a visible and auditable source-to-interpretation chain, richer user constraints, explicit uncertainty and abstention, feasible verification/monitoring choices, and total attention cost.
sources.verified_findings: Evaluation text assesses enhanced summary overlap and keyword-based article selection. The inspected method/limitations do not establish improved investment outcomes. Authors explicitly characterize generated recommendations as preliminary insights requiring further analysis.
sources.numeric_result: Not reported here; headline BLEU/ROUGE and '40%' relevance improvement are not used without auditing evaluation references and denominator.
sources.limitations: Keyword-level personalization, obligatory three recommendations, context truncation, and no established investment-decision benefit in the inspected evaluation. Independent proceedings metadata and outcome evaluation remain unverified; use it as a closely overlapping system precedent rather than efficacy evidence.
sources.nubble_upgrade: Permit zero recommendations. Require action preconditions, owner, resource constraints and evidence sufficiency; compare to this staged prompt baseline with identical source/context/token budgets.

sources.title: Comparative Personalization for Multi-document Summarization
sources.evidence_level: A for method/limitations; numeric outcome comparisons not extracted
evidence_sections: Appendix author attribution and factuality evaluation
sources.core_method: Compares a user's authored documents to same-topic documents by others to derive a structured style/content profile; uses it for MDS. AuthorMap evaluates personalization by authorship attribution; PerMSum supplies news and review data.
sources.closest_overlap: Structured user analysis as an intermediate representation and personalized multidocument summarization already exist.
sources.defensible_difference: Author identity/style discrimination differs from reader-goal fulfillment and decision usefulness. No explicit conditional action layer is established in the inspected passages.
sources.verified_findings: Authors report stronger personalization than baselines; no numerical superiority claim reproduced here. They explicitly limit generalization because comparable same-topic documents may be unavailable, and news profiles are authored texts rather than clicked/liked texts.
sources.limitations: Authorship match may reward style or ideology without improving usefulness; factuality assessed separately.
sources.nubble_upgrade: Keep content relevance, action quality and writing style as separate evaluation dimensions. Use counterfactual users with different constraints to test whether recommendations change for a justified reason.

sources.title: Is Summary Useful or Not? An Extrinsic Human Evaluation of Text Summaries on Downstream Tasks
sources.version_read: arXiv v1 (2023-05-24), with LREC-COLING 2024 title/authors/abstract checked
sources.publication_status: Published conference paper; inspected arXiv version predates proceedings
sources.evidence_level: A: canonical proceedings metadata plus primary experimental protocol/results in preprint; version distinction retained
sources.core_method: Measures human QA, text classification and text-similarity performance and time using original articles or similarly sized summaries; tests intrinsic metric agreement with extrinsic utility.
sources.closest_overlap: Directly measures what people can do after reading and time savings; this should be a methodological foundation rather than claimed novelty.
sources.defensible_difference: The task is not professional implication/action selection and lacks Nubble's linked representations and explicit abstention.
sources.verified_findings: In the inspected preprint, summaries reduce task time by approximately 61–62% in QA, 59% in classification and 42% in similarity, while QA performance worsens; task accuracy and time must therefore be reported separately.
sources.numeric_result: Percentages above are author-reported Table 2–3 comparisons for their setup, not expected Nubble gains. Protocol describes campus graduate participants aged 22–26; separate recruitment for source-based QA.
sources.limitations: Task-specific generalization and restricted participant population; reference-based versus source-based QA yields different conclusions.
sources.nubble_upgrade: Use a quality–time frontier and equal-budget primary comparison, report errors as well as speed, and sample questions independently of generated summary content.

sources.title: Re-FRAME the Meeting Summarization SCOPE: Fact-Based Summarization and Personalization via Questions
sources.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2025
sources.version_read: arXiv v2, 2025-11-14; canonical proceedings metadata rechecked 2026-10-25
sources.publication_status: Published proceedings paper; canonical metadata rechecked 2026-10-25
sources.evidence_level: A for primary method/evaluation passage reading; canonical arXiv version date not independently checked
sources.core_method: Extracts statement–context fact tuples, selects/scorers facts, organizes and synthesizes. SCOPE elicits model representations of a reader's knowledge, project, goals, urgency, comprehension needs, relevance and uncertainty before selection.
sources.closest_overlap: Strong precedent for source-grounded intermediate facts plus goal-, context- and knowledge-aware relevance; explicitly tests goal alignment and prioritization.
sources.defensible_difference: Meeting summarization does not itself establish Nubble's prospective conditional implication, feasible action/verify/monitor/no-action alternatives or equal-time decision benefit.
sources.verified_findings: P-MESA is an LLM-based seven-dimension evaluation with a human calibration study. Inspected Table 1 reports per-dimension balanced detection accuracies 89.1–93.3% and Spearman correlations 0.70–0.81. These validate that specific evaluator setup, not real decision outcomes.
sources.numeric_result: Do not transplant P-MESA scores into Nubble claims; table read only to verify evaluator design and boundaries.
sources.limitations: Reader fit as judged by P-MESA is a proxy, not demonstrated downstream utility. Nine-question generation protocol is not a guarantee that reader assumptions are correct.
sources.nubble_upgrade: Represent user context explicitly, allow correction, and separate human calibration of relevance from human evaluation of action quality; include goal/knowledge/urgency ablations.

sources.title: Information Satisfaction: A Reader-Centered Axis for Summarization Evaluation
sources.venue: ACM publication linked by DOI; exact conference name not established from inspected metadata
sources.version_read: arXiv v1 (2026-08-14); matching ACM full text verified
sources.publication_status: ACM publication exists with matching DOI/title/full text; precise venue label not verified
sources.access_level: Open primary arXiv and ACM full text
sources.evidence_level: A: arXiv metadata, matching ACM full text, primary perturbation and human protocol passages
evidence_sections: §4 self-reported persona, real query, same context and blinded tournament
sources.core_method: Defines reader information satisfaction using query plus persona; tests metric sensitivity to distractors, incremental content, content-preserving length changes and audience shifts. Human study uses reader-owned expertise/use cases and real queries, fixed retrieved context, and a 2×2 model/persona prompt design.
sources.closest_overlap: Reader-specific informational utility and role/knowledge context are explicitly established. Even persona-conditioned LLM judges can fail to capture what the individual reader needs.
sources.defensible_difference: Information satisfaction differs from correct, feasible prospective decisions under an attention budget; Nubble must evaluate both rather than assume one implies the other.
sources.verified_findings: The primary text reports poor automatic-metric agreement with reader preferences, including persona-conditioned judges; no general Nubble validity follows from a rubric alone.
sources.numeric_result: Not reported here; avoid 'no metric exceeds chance' without reproducing their exact comparison and statistical test.
sources.limitations: Queries retrieve paper abstracts; scope is information satisfaction rather than action or real-world outcome.
sources.nubble_upgrade: Adopt audience-swap and content-preserving length perturbations as construct checks; use real users' self-reported contexts and goals, fixed evidence bundles, blinded paired preference, and an independent task-performance endpoint.

excluded_or_followup.title: Decision-Oriented Text Evaluation
excluded_or_followup.reason: Read primary methods/results/limitations; useful adjacent financial decision-evaluation precedent but weak for efficacy because only three human annotators and narrow short-term market setup. Bibliography misidentifies DecSum's author and DOI. Not used as independent corroboration.

excluded_or_followup.title: Improving meeting summarization by focusing on user needs: a task-oriented evaluation
excluded_or_followup.reason: Important historical candidate discovered through metadata search; full text not read here, so no empirical claims included.

excluded_or_followup.title: Extrinsic summarization evaluation: A decision audit task
excluded_or_followup.reason: Historical candidate discovered; conference/journal variants and full text not resolved here. Do not cite from this record without bibliographic verification.

claim_limits: This is not an exhaustive or systematic search.
Versions of the same paper are not independent evidence.
No reviewed study establishes Nubble's effectiveness.
Absence of a feature from inspected passages is a qualified comparison, not proof that no prior system has it.
Publication statuses are what was verified on 2026-10-25; preprint existence is not peer review.
Source metadata does not confer permission to redistribute source documents or datasets.
